title: Mutation rate heterogeneity biases variant effect prediction and reveals genuine mutational robustness.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: paper_context.py: no PMCID, not open access in Europe PMC, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links, no Zenodo/Dryad hit on the DOI. Web searches (4) found no preprint, GitHub repository or data deposit for this paper; a CRG (Centre for Genomic Regulation) press article mentions none either.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From abstract and press coverage only: 50 VEPs (variant effect predictors) evaluated on ~13.5 million mutations across 6,659 human genes, plus protein-stability measurements from the Lehner lab (~500 human protein domains, i.e. the Human Domainome). None of these numbers were checked in files.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited dataset, supplement or code link found; the paper is paywalled with no PMC copy. It is an analysis of existing public resources (precomputed VEP scores, mutation-rate maps, Domainome stability), not a new dataset.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Any ML project would have to assemble its own table by joining VEP scores, a per-site mutation-rate model and stability measurements on genomic coordinates; no ready label table from this paper.

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper claims ~13.5M mutations, but no count was verified in any file.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not checked; genome-wide VEP score tables (e.g. dbNSFP-scale) would be tens of GB.

a8_label_provenance.note: The paper's main quantity is other models' outputs (VEP scores) regressed on modelled mutation rates, so it is model-on-model; only the stability arm traces to a physical measurement, and that data belongs to a different paper.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (for a hypothetical mutation-rate-aware stability model)

integration.partner_dataset: Human Domainome stability data (MaveDB) plus a per-site mutation-rate map such as Roulette
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does adding explicit mutation probability to a variant effect predictor remove the bias toward calling rare-mutation sites damaging?

honest_claim_h3: Not applicable: there is no dataset from this paper to model; the paper is a bias analysis of existing predictors.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence plus how likely each mutation is to arise to predict how damaging it is, without mistaking rarity for harm.
plain_idea.train_on: Single amino-acid changes in human protein domains with measured stability, each annotated with its estimated mutation rate; count unknown because this paper deposits no table.
plain_idea.predict: Measured change in protein stability (from the Lehner lab's Human Domainome experiments), and whether the prediction stays unbiased across mutation-rate bins.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinical geneticists rely on predictors that, per this paper, rate low-mutation-rate sites as more damaging than they are; a corrected predictor would change variant interpretation.

ml_idea: A mutation-rate-aware variant effect predictor trained on Human Domainome stability data with mutation-rate covariates. It would need to be built from the Domainome deposit and a mutation-rate map, not from this paper, so it should be evaluated as a separate candidate.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data from this paper to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for a data or code availability statement in the AJHG article; none was found in Europe PMC or by web search.

verdict_reason: A1/A2 fail: a paywalled analysis paper with no deposited data, supplement or code found. Its quantities are other models' scores joined to mutation-rate maps, so any label table would have to be built from other resources. The real data source, the Human Domainome, should be evaluated on its own.
